output.brief:
The October shortfalls were caused by a configuration change, not by your data. On 22 Oct an Ardentra consultant applied a standard template to the night premium rule NSP-02. The change log called it a label correction with no effect on pay. The platform's audit trail shows it also moved the premium start time from 20:00 to 22:00. Internal audit recalculated pay for all 158 night workers. 147 were underpaid, and each shortfall equals the premium for the 20:00–22:00 hours. The 11 people paid correctly work 22:00–06:00. Re-running October in the test tenant with 20:00 restored matched expected pay for all 158. Ardentra's data account doesn't hold up. The extract it names (MD-1023) was never loaded, and flagged records were no more likely to be underpaid than unflagged ones. I'm fairly sure of this (about 90%).
Recommended actions:
- Don't suspend the HR team or re-cleanse the data, and don't accept the clause 14.3 cost.
- Have Ardentra restore the 20:00 start before 24 Nov. Verify it, then pay all 147 underpaid staff off-cycle. 8 of them raised no ticket.
- Don't roll back release 7.4.
- Keep the rota trial under review. The evidence doesn't show whether the pay error or the trial caused the fall in overtime cover.
- Ask why the change was recorded as having no pay impact and was never tested.
